findings.why: The inverted syntax "It had gone through him too, that a single question had taken..." made me backtrack to figure out what 'it' referred to before the sentence resolved.
"his own he would take last" inverts normal word order and I had to pause to parse it as 'he would take his own [pleasure] last.'

The sentence stacks 'She could have been Randi' onto a long causal clause about 'grammar' as metaphor, and I had to reread to connect the dash-clause back to what was actually being claimed about his expectations.

This is a verbless fragment listing descriptors ("Sex-kitten, the trailing register, a hand light on his arm") and I had to reread it against the surrounding dialogue to figure out it was characterizing how the previous line was delivered.

The piled-up negations ('not before, not to be told... but after...') followed by a colon into an italicized internal question made me lose the thread of what was being described and I had to re-read to reconnect it to 'She looked at him then.'
The sentence opens with a long noun phrase ('A decade of dance and three years of...') before any verb arrives, so I had to hold it in suspension waiting for the clause to resolve.
